items.event_time_ist: Lawsuit filed Oct 2, 2026; NAACP press release Oct 5, 2026
items.summary: Catch-up missed by earlier runs: the NAACP sued the DOJ's Civil Rights Division head Harmeet Dhillon (filed in D.C. federal court Friday, Oct 2, 2026; press release Oct 5) over plans to deploy roughly 1,000 federal 'election monitors' to midterm polling sites in all 50 states — the largest such deployment ever (vs ~289 in 2022 and 714 in 2024). It's a FOIA-records suit seeking emergency disclosure of legal authority, personnel, training and deployment locations after DOJ didn't answer a Sept 1 FOIA request; it does NOT ask the court to block the monitors. Filed Oct 5: motion for temporary restraining order. NAACP cites the August Wyoming primary incident where GOP Gov. Mark Gordon called DOJ monitors 'aggressive' and 'irregular' and alleged attempts to inspect voting machines. Corroborated by Democracy Docket (original reporting) + The Guardian (Adam Gabbatt original) + NAACP release = confirmed.
items.title: NAACP sues DOJ over plan to deploy ~1,000 federal 'election monitors' to midterm polling sites
